walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1973 Structure of Atonal Music codified set classes?
options: Forte
Lewin
Babbitt
Rahn

mcqs.q: Whose 1998 Classical Form defines thematic functions?
options: Caplin
Hepokoski
Webster
Rosen

mcqs.q: What is a tone row in serial music?
options: An ordered series of all 12 chromatic pitches, used as the basis of a piece.
A row of notes played together as a chord.
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
Vibrato on a single note.
Rapid alternation between the written note and the note a step above.
Three notes played at once.

mcqs.q: How many semitones are in a perfect fifth?
options: 5 (counting letter-name positions).
Three notes played at once.
